actions.title: Write down one goal
actions.description: Name what the money is for, how much you need, and when you expect to need it.
actions.relevance: A clear amount and date give you something concrete to plan toward, before considering products.

actions.title: Check how you can access your money
actions.description: Find the withdrawal time, restrictions, and any early-access penalties for an account you use or are researching.
actions.relevance: Money that exists on paper may not be available when you need it. Keep planned expenses separate from an emergency buffer.

actions.title: Describe what a loss would mean for your goal
actions.description: Separate how you feel about price swings from whether a loss could affect essential expenses or delay your goal.
actions.relevance: Being comfortable with uncertainty does not remove a need for money at a particular time.

actions.title: Find out what a product actually holds
actions.description: Look for an official holdings list. Note the largest companies, industries, or regions and anything you do not understand.
actions.relevance: Different product names do not necessarily mean different underlying investments. Diversification reduces risk but cannot remove it.

actions.title: Find the fees in an official document
actions.description: Find the annual percentage charge for an option you are researching. Note transaction costs and other charges separately.
actions.relevance: Small recurring charges can change long-term outcomes, but fees alone do not tell you whether an option is suitable.

actions.title: Choose what to review after a life change
actions.description: Write down which goal dates, access needs, or responsibilities you would revisit after a change in circumstances.
actions.relevance: A plan is a set of assumptions to review, not a permanent investor identity. Retirement spending needs more analysis than a simple savings projection.
